title: ‘Robocop’ TV Series Casts Dan Stevens in Lead Role
description:
Dan Stevens is set for the title role in the “Robocop” TV series at Amazon Prime Video, Variety has confirmed. 

	The show was originally announced
body:
Dan Stevens is set for the title role in the “Robocop” TV series at Amazon Prime Video, Variety has confirmed. 

	The show was originally announced in July at the streamer. Prime Video has given the show an eight-episode order. The project has been in development since Amazon acquired MGM in 2022, with Amazon looking to capitalize on their access to MGM’s deep IP library for both film and television projects.


	Per the official logline, “A giant tech conglomerate convinces the city to place a powerful robot on its police force – a robot implanted with the consciousness of a beloved, fallen officer (Stevens).”
	

	Stevens broke out with his role in the hit British series “Downton Abbey,” with the actor going on to star in the critically-acclaimed show “Legion” at FX. His other TV roles include “Solar Opposites,” “Zero Day,” and the upcoming third season of AMC’s “The Terror.” He is also set for a series regular role in the upcoming second season of “Dexter: Resurrection.” In film, he recently starred in “Godzilla x Kong: New Empire” and is known for features like the live-action “Beauty and the Beast,” “Eurovision Song Contest: The Story of Fire Saga,” and “Cuckoo.”

	He is repped by CAA, Julian Belfrage Associates, and Peikoff Mahan.

	Peter Ocko serves as writer, executive producer, and showrunner. James Wan, Michael Clear, and Rob Hackett executive produce via Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Michael Miner and Ed Neumeier, co-creators and co-writers of the original “Robocop” film, will also serve as executive producers. Danielle Bozzone of Blumhouse Atomic Monster will co-executive produce and oversee the project for the company. Amazon MGM Studios will produce.
	

	The “Robocop” franchise kicked off in 1987 with the first film starring Peter Weller as the titular half man, half machine law enforcement officer. Weller returned for the sequel in 1990, with Robert Burke taking over the role for “Robocop 3” in 1993. Nancy Allen starred in all three films as Officer Anne Lewis. A reboot starring Joel Kinnaman was released in 2014. There have also been multiple “Robocop” TV shows to date, including two animated and two live-action shows, as well as video games and comic books.

schema.headline: ‘Robocop’ TV Series Casts Dan Stevens in Lead Role

title: Andrew Garfield Opens Up About Playing Sam Altman in ‘Artificial,’ Says OpenAI Is Doing ‘Damage to the Soul of Humanity’
description:
Andrew Garfield is opening up about stepping into the shoes of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film “Artificial.”

	Garfield por
body:
Andrew Garfield is opening up about stepping into the shoes of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming film “Artificial.”

	Garfield portrays the tech executive in the drama, which takes place during the five-day corporate saga in November 2023 that saw Altman abruptly fired as OpenAI CEO before ultimately returning to the company. In a new interview with Esquire U.K., Garfield stressed that his portrayal isn’t based on any personal relationship with Altman.
	

	“I don’t know Sam Altman. I’ve never met him,” Garfield said. “I was going off of the script and court transcripts and interviews and research, and we were telling a story. But I think anyone who takes on that level of responsibility for a company or a technology that you know is going to do a hell of a lot of damage to the soul of humanity [must have] a certain ability to dissociate.”


	Garfield also said his usual acting process required him to look for elements of Altman within himself, including traits he might rather reject. He described the exercise using Carl Jung’s concept of “the shadow self,” or, as Garfield put it, “the aspects of ourselves that we disown.”

	“There’s something there for me to integrate, because I’m so afraid of being it,” he said.

	“But then the argument is, that if we weren’t all less rejecting in the first place, less ‘that’s not us’, then Donald Trump wouldn’t have been voted in twice, and Nigel Farage wouldn’t be anywhere near a position of power,” he continued. “Whereas if we go, ‘OK, interesting — where am I [in a] wannabe fascist, grifter, opportunist, power-hungry, ethic-less, spineless fucking pig?’ We can identify that this is the bad part of us. We know this in ourselves.”
	

	“Artificial,” written by Simon Rich, also stars Monica Barbaro as former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, Yura Borisov as OpenAI co-founder and former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever and Ike Barinholtz as Elon Musk. Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman, Billie Lourd, Zosia Mamet, Chris O’Dowd and Mark Rylance round out the ensemble.

	wn. Amazon MGM Studios, which originally developed and financed the roughly $40 million project, dropped “Artificial” in June after principal photography had been completed. The move came months after Amazon announced a major investment in OpenAI. Amazon said at the time that it believed the film would be “better served if it were released by a different studio.”

	Neon subsequently acquired worldwide theatrical rights to the film.

schema.headline: Andrew Garfield Opens Up About Playing Sam Altman in ‘Artificial,’ Says OpenAI Is Doing ‘Damage to the Soul of Humanity’

body:
Prepare to reenter high society, because “The Gilded Age” has set its Season 4 premiere date at HBO. 

	The fourth season of the period drama will debut on Nov. 1 on HBO and HBO Max at 9 pm ET/PT. HBO has also released a new teaser for the season, which can be seen below. 

	The official logline for Season 4 states, “Bertha Russell (Carrie Coon) changed Society at a cost. Now, her family must reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) seizes an opportunity to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) forges a new path for herself, and Peggy (Denée Benton) works to be accepted by her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.” 
	

	The expansive cast for Season 4 also includes: Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Taissa Farmiga, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Ben Ahlers, Ashlie Atkinson, Dylan Baker, Kelley Curran, Jordan Donica, Jessica Frances Dukes, Amy Forsyth, Jack Gilpin, Simon Jones, Celia Keenan-Bolger, Ben Lamb, Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Debra Monk, Hattie Morahan, Donna Murphy, Kristine Nielsen, Kelli O’Hara, Taylor Richardson, Douglas Sills, Erin Wilhelmi, John Douglas Thompson, Taylor Trensch, James Scully, Dennis Haysbert, Maggie Kuntz, Neal Huff, Bonnie Milligan, Jim Gaffigan, Dallas Roberts, Andrew Burnap, Elizabeth Marvel, Adrienne Warren, with Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad.


	Julian Fellowes created “The Gilded Age” and serves as writer and executive producer. Salli Richardson-Whitfield seres as director and executiev producer, with Sonja Warfield writing and executive producing. Gareth Neame, David Crockett, Bob Greenblatt, Kate Churchill, Davita Scarlett, and Elaine Aronson also executive produce. Erica Armstrong Dunbar and Holly Rymon co-executive produce. The series is co-produced by HBO and Universal Television.

title: Paramount’s Brit Network 5 Being Sued by Producer Blackbox Multimedia Over Shelved Drama Series
description: Paramount‘s U.K. network 5 is being sued by one of its production partners over what the company claims was the “wrongful termination” of an agreeme
body:
Paramount‘s U.K. network 5 is being sued by one of its production partners over what the company claims was the “wrongful termination” of an agreement over a crime drama series. 

	Blackbox Multimedia, the U.K. banner that has made series for 5 such as “The Ex-Wife” and “Benidorm is Murder,” claims that it is owned money by the channel, which was acquired by Paramount in 2014. 

	According to lawyers representing Blackbox, the case revolves around a drama that that was originally to be based on true events. 
	

	Blackbox asserts that it was approached by 5, which asked it to come aboard as a producer on the project, which had already been conceived by the channel and a third-party, which had the pre-existing relationship with the individual at the center of the events. 


	“Blackbox established early in development that the individual did not wish to participate or for the story to be based on her experiences. Channel 5 was aware of this from a very early stage,” said Blackbox’s legal representatives in a statement to Variety. “Accordingly, and in full consultation with Channel 5, Blackbox developed the project into a wholly fictional drama. No character, relationship or storyline in the series is based on or intended to represent any specific individual or real case.”

	But Blackbox claims that the drama was not finalized or delivered “only because Channel 5 wrongfully terminated the agreement.” As as result, it says that it “has been left carrying the financial burden of Channel 5’s wrongful termination.”

	According to Variety‘s sister publication Deadline, which first broke news of the court case, 5 denies that Blackbox ever delivered the drama and that it pulled the series following a complaint by an individual connected to the project, who had claimed that the drama was affecting their safety and wellbeing. 
	

	It added that 5 said it was not made aware of such claims by Blackbox before production commenced and felt it had no choice to walk away because of duty of care. Variety has reached out to 5 for comment. 

	In its statement to Variety, Blackbox’s lawyers said that litigation was “very much a last resort,” adding that the company was a “long-standing and trusted production partner to Channel 5.”

schema.headline: Paramount’s Brit Network 5 Being Sued by Producer Blackbox Multimedia Over Shelved Drama Series

title: Oscars: Germany Selects Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’ for International Feature Race
description:
Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime” has been selected as Germany’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film.

	The film’s synopsis r
body:
Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime” has been selected as Germany’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film.

	The film’s synopsis reads as follows: The last photograph Jessie took shows the sun over Berlin. It hangs there as if nothing had happened. But Ella has lost her daughter. What remains is Jessie’s younger sister and a complicated relationship with the boy everyone blames. The unlikely trio ends up on a family holiday that never really existed. Under the shimmering sun of Tenerife, memory and the present become inseparably intertwined. The ghosts are everywhere.
	

	“Everytime” celebrated its world premiere at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in May. Wollner’s third feature film, for which she also wrote the screenplay, was selected for the Un Certain Regard sidebar where it won the Prix Un Certain Regard, the section’s top award. Cannes was followed by invitations to the Sydney Film Festival and the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, among others. At the Sarajevo Film Festival, “Everytime” was awarded the Heart of Sarajevo Grand Prize. Its North American premiere will follow in September at the Toronto Film Festival. Other festival appearances include the New York Film Festival.


	Germany’s Oscar jury said, “In ‘Everytime,’ director and writer Sandra Wollner achieves the remarkable feat of making grief tangible as a world thrown into disarray through purely cinematic means and with a surprising lightness of touch. The outstanding cinematography creates a shimmering and at times ethereal atmosphere without intruding on the characters. The ensemble of actors is convincing in its naturalness, with the characterizations remaining consistently precise and ambivalent. Playing elegantly with form and narrative ellipses, ‘Everytime’ explores the interstices of the pain of loss. Memory and the present, reality and imagination flow into one another almost imperceptibly, making this film a truly poetic cinematic experience.”
	

	German distributor Eksystent Filmverleih Kijas released “Everytime” in German cinemas on Aug. 6. Charades is handling international sales. It was sold to more than 30 territories worldwide. In North America, 1-2 Special is handling distribution, with a theatrical release planned for early 2027.

	Due to a change in the rules of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences this spring, two major German films are already eligible for submission in the international feature film category: Visar Morina’s “Shame and Money” qualified by winning the Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival, as did İlker Çatak’s “Yellow Letters” by winning the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival.

	The 15-title shortlist of eligible films for the international feature film Oscar race will be announced on Dec. 15. The five nominated titles that will enter the race will be revealed on Jan. 21. The Academy Awards ceremony will take place on March 14.

schema.headline: Oscars: Germany Selects Sandra Wollner’s ‘Everytime’ for International Feature Race

title: Following Oscars Success, CNN and Variety to Partner Again for Emmys Red Carpet Pre-Show
description:
Last awards season, Variety and CNN partnered on the Oscars red carpet, Actors on Actors and a one-of-a-kind town hall with Timothée Chalamet. 

	No
body:
Last awards season, Variety and CNN partnered on the Oscars red carpet, Actors on Actors and a one-of-a-kind town hall with Timothée Chalamet. 

	Now, this fall, the two venerable brands are teaming up again. CNN and Variety will deliver exclusive live pre-show coverage from the red carpet of the 78th Emmy Awards.

	CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh will serve as hosts for the event, titled “CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV’s Biggest Night.” The stream airs on Monday, Sept. 14, at 5 p.m. ET on CNN.com/watch and on the CNN app for CNN’s streaming subscribers.
	



	

	



	Wagmeister and Setoodeh last appeared together as hosts of the Oscar pre-show in March. The duo, industry veterans and former colleagues at Variety, will bring their deep knowledge and expertise of all things Hollywood to deliver up-to-the-minute commentary on TV’s biggest party. The stream will feature exclusive interviews and must-see moments.


	“CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV’s Biggest Night” expands a partnership that most recently produced the latest season of the Daytime Emmy-nominated “Actors on Actors” franchise. Season 24 featured talent at the center of this year’s Emmy Awards, including host and nominee Mariska Hargitay and nominees Jamie Lee Curtis, Colman Domingo, Sally Field, Claire Danes, Lisa Kudrow, Noah Wyle, Sarah Pidgeon and Rhea Seehorn. This season drew strong audiences for CNN, and ranked among the top drivers of new CNN All Access subscriptions in June during its premiere.
	

	Wagmeister’s own awards coverage through her new CNN series “Coming Up,” featuring interviews with Emmy-nominated actors, can be streamed now at CNN.com/watch and on the CNN app for CNN’s streaming subscribers.

	The 78th Emmy Awards air live Monday, Sept. 14, from 8 p.m. to 11 p.m. ET on NBC and streaming on Peacock.

schema.headline: Following Oscars Success, CNN and Variety to Partner Again for Emmys Red Carpet Pre-Show

title: ‘The Rookie’ Creator Alexi Hawley Extends Overall Deal With Lionsgate TV, as His Drama Project ‘The Envoy’ Moves to HBO Max
description: “The Rookie” creator Alexi Hawley has sealed a new, multi-year overall deal with Lionsgate Television — extending a pact he first made with the stud
body:
“The Rookie” creator Alexi Hawley has sealed a new, multi-year overall deal with Lionsgate Television — extending a pact he first made with the studio in 2024. The extension continues the writer/producer/showrunner’s work on “The Rookie” franchise while also developing and producing new scripted TV series for Lionsgate.

	“The Rookie,” about to enter its Season 9, first launched on ABC in October 2018; at the time, it was produced by eOne Television. Lionsgate has been the show’s studio since Season 6 (2024), after its acquisition of eOne studio assets. “The Rookie” previously spawned the spinoff “The Rookie: Feds,” and now has the upcoming ABC spinoff “The Rookie: North,” starring Jay Ellis, coming next season.
	

	Hawley serves as showrunner on both “The Rookie” and “The Rookie: North.” Next up, he’s developing “The Envoy” for HBO Max, from Lionsgate TV. The show, adapted from a Vanity Fair article by Adam Ciralsky, was previously set up at Hulu.


	Ciralsky is also an exec producer on the show, which looks at “Roger Carstens and his team at the State Department who brought home 70 American hostages during his four-year tenure as Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs. The article details an in-depth look at the U.S. government’s commitment to freeing hostages.”

	Hawley is an EP on “The Envoy” with Carstens also serving as an executive producer. Ciralsky is an EP through his P3 Media banner, with Gene Klein an EP as well.

	“Alexi has built ‘The Rookie’ into one of broadcast television’s strongest and most enduring franchises, with a flagship series that continues to grow and a compelling new chapter on the horizon with ‘The Rookie: North,’” said Lionsgate TV Group chair/chief creative officer Kevin Beggs in a statement. “He has a remarkable ability to create characters and stories that resonate with audiences year after year and bring a new generation of viewers into the franchise. We’re excited to continue our partnership as we grow ‘The Rookie’ franchise and bring Alexi’s new projects to the screen.”
	

	Hawley’s past projects with Lionsgate include Netflix’s spy thriller “The Recruit,” starring Noah Centineo, which ran for two seasons on the streamer. (Ciralsky was an EP with Hawley on that series too.)

	In a statement, Hawley called Lionsgate “an invaluable creative partner and a strong champion of my work. I’m drawn to stories that are propulsive and entertaining, while still grounded in deeply human characters and real emotional stakes. I look forward to continuing to build on our work together while bringing new ideas and ambitious stories to the studio in the years ahead.” 

	Hawley is repped by The Shuman Company and Hansen Jacobsen Teller.

schema.headline: ‘The Rookie’ Creator Alexi Hawley Extends Overall Deal With Lionsgate TV, as His Drama Project ‘The Envoy’ Moves to HBO Max

title: Netflix Sets Norm Macdonald Documentary From Judd Apatow, Plus Three More Comedy Docs in October (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
At Netflix, October isn’t just for scary movies; it’s also for funny documentaries.

	The streamer will premiere four feature docs celebrating some
body:
At Netflix, October isn’t just for scary movies; it’s also for funny documentaries.

	The streamer will premiere four feature docs celebrating some of comedy’s most influential voices and institutions, with one film rolling out each week in October.

	Debuting on Oct. 7 is “Who Is Martin Mull?,” from the late Bob Saget and Neil Berkeley. The film tells the story of the Chicago-born actor, musician and painter known for “Mary Hartman, Mary Hartman” and for playing Gene Parmesan on “Arrested Development.” Per the logline, it “traces his restless reinvention from smoky folk clubs to primetime sitcoms to gallery walls, told in his own words and by the friends who watched it happen, including Steve Martin, Tom Waits, David Alan Grier and others.” The film is produced by Sean Bradley, Tara Billik and Berkeley and executive produced by Kevin S. Bright, Saget, Morgan Neville and Caitrin Rogers.
	



	

					Who Is Martin Mull? Martin Mull in Who Is Martin Mull?. Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026
									Courtesy of Netflix
	



	Next is Judd Apatow‘s previously announced Norm Macdonald documentary, which premieres on Oct. 16. “Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald” is an intimate portrait of the “Saturday Night Live” legend, chronicling “his rise as the deadpan anchor of “Weekend Update” to his enduring legacy as a comedian’s comedian — a master of the absurd, the dry, and the unexpected,” per the logline. The doc is built entirely from archival footage, personal photos and rare home videos. (Last year, Apatow solicited “unique photos and videos of Norm” from fans on Instagram.) It’s produced by Apatow, Amanda Rohlke and Ross M. Dinerstein. EPs are Josh Church, Marc Gurvitz, Jon Liebman, Zoe Rogovin, Mark McCune and Ross Girard.
	

	A Maria Bamford documentary from Apatow and Berkeley is coming to Netflix on Oct. 23. “Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story,” which first premiered at Sundance earlier this year, is a funny and tender glimpse into the childhood, early career and present-day life of a comedy great, who is known for “turning radical honesty into radical comedy — often blurring the line between performance and personal crisis.” Producing alongside Apatow and Berkeley are Amanda Rohlke and David Heiman. Josh Church, Wayne Federman and Olivia Rosenbloom executive produce.



	

					Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story. (L-R) Marilyn Bamford, Maria Bamford, and Joel Bamford in Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story. Cr. NETFLIX © 2026
									COURTESY OF NETFLIX
	



	Lastly, on Oct. 30 comes “SCTV: The Greatest Show You’ve Never Heard Of.” The documentary, from Jason Hehir, the director of the Michael Jordan miniseries “The Last Dance,” tells the story of one of the most influential sketch comedy series in TV history. “Second City Television” helped boost the careers of John Candy, Eugene Levy, Martin Short, Catherine O’Hara, Rick Moranis and more future comedy greats. “Through intimate interviews with surviving members of its legendary cast and an emotional reunion in Toronto, the film explores the creative partnership that transformed a small Canadian television production into a cultural phenomenon that launched some of comedy’s most celebrated icons,” according to the description. The film promises never-before-shared stories and rare archival material. Chapman Downes, Whitney Johnson, Andrew Hafnor, Molly Montgomery and Kelly Meinhardt are executive producers.

	In addition to the upcoming SCTV documentary, all episodes of “Second City TV” will be arriving on Netflix starting on Sept. 1.



	

					SCTV, clockwise from top left: Joe Flaherty as Guy Caballero, Andrea Martin as Edith Prickley (center), Catherine O’hara as Lola Heatherton, John Candy as  Johnny LaRue, Eugene Levy as Bobby Bittman, Martin Short as Ed Grimley, Rick Moranis as Bob MacKenzie, 1976-1981
									Courtesy Everett Collection

schema.headline: Netflix Sets Norm Macdonald Documentary From Judd Apatow, Plus Three More Comedy Docs in October (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Paul Thomas Anderson’s ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Concert Movie Acquired by Janus Films, Criterion
description: Janus Films and Criterion have acquired North American rights to “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall,” a concert film shot and directed by Paul Thomas
body:
Janus Films and Criterion have acquired North American rights to “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall,” a concert film shot and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson.

	The concert was captured on 35mm and 16mm film during a sold-out solo performance from the Geese frontman at Carnegie Hall in December 2025. Geese kicked off its Getting Killed world tour in October 2025. The band’s third headlining tour concludes in November.


	The music for “Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall” was recorded and produced for the film and live album from music producer Ariel Rechtshaid. The live album will be released Oct. 9 from Partisan Records and Play It Again Sam.
	

	The film is co-produced by Bennie Safdie and produced by Sara Murphy, Erica Frauman and Maggie Ambrose.

	Winter has been the frontman for Geese since it formed in 2016. The band’s breakthrough album, “Getting Killed,” was released by Partisan Records and Play It Again Sam in 2025. He released his debut solo album, “Heavy Metal,” in 2024.

	The concert film’s roadshow engagements in theaters start Nov. 20. Tickets go on sale Sept. 17. The film tour’s dates are below:

title: ‘Dunkman’: How Shaquille O’Neal Made Dunk Contests Great Again
description:
Shaquille O’Neal loves solving problems.

	The basketball icon and four-time NBA champion, 54, has two master’s degrees, a doctorate, served as a sh
body:
Shaquille O’Neal loves solving problems.

	The basketball icon and four-time NBA champion, 54, has two master’s degrees, a doctorate, served as a sheriff’s deputy and honorary U.S. Marshal, and once played for Doc Rivers.

	Back in 2016, the basketball icon needed to install a home security system only to have a company quote him $60,000 to $80,000. During one of his routine trips to Best Buy — his favorite store — he spotted the Ring Doorbell Camera for sale at a fraction of the price and decided to give it a whirl.  
	

	“I went to China the next week and thought, ‘Damn, this thing works in China!’” O’Neal recalls to Variety.


	He began hounding Colin Smeeton, his longtime manager and business partner, about meeting the owner of Ring and investing in the company. The following January, O’Neal made a beeline for Ring founder Jamie Siminoff at CES, the annual tech trade show in Las Vegas, telling him, “I’d love to find a way to partner with you but I don’t want to just be a pitchman; I want to have equity in the company.” So, O’Neal was granted what Smeeton calls “a sizable equity stake in the company” that made him millions when it sold to Amazon for $1.15 billion a year later.

	“He’s constantly challenging himself and always looking for what the new opportunity is,” Smeeton says.

	O’Neal sensed a similar opportunity with the NBA Slam Dunk Contest.



	

					A scene from “Dunkman.”
									TNT
	



	It had been close to a decade since the annual All-Star Weekend competition was any good (see: Zach LaVine vs. Aaron Gordon, 2016), and a quarter-century removed from the last bona fide NBA superstar participating in it (Vince Carter, 2000). The days of Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant soaring through the air were long gone.
	

	“All the best dunkers in the NBA were not showing up, and when I was growing up, the best dunkers were in the NBA,” explains O’Neal. “I would definitely up the prize money. I’d put a Ferrari in the middle of the floor for first place and a Rolls-Royce for second place.”  

	He continues, “The last great dunk contest we had was Zach LaVine and Aaron Gordon… But then I would scroll through the internet and see these kids do dunks and look at their big [social media] followings, so me and my partners were like, ‘Let’s create a dunk league to put these guys together.’”

	The result is “Dunkman,” a live televised competition where 24 of the world’s best dunkers spin and slam their way to a $500,000 grand prize, the largest in the history of competitive dunking (and $125,000 for second place). Airing across TNT and HBO Max, and presented by Authentic Studios and TNT Sports, “Dunkman” has proven to be a social media sensation, attracting over 854 million social views across platforms during its group stages. The final will air the night of Aug. 25.

	And yes, there may not be NBA superstars jamming it home on “Dunkman” but you do have the unique privilege of seeing a 5-foot-9 furniture salesman from Utah with a nearly 50-inch vertical leap (Hyrum “Hyt Check” Fechser) dunk over several men on a couch and send O’Neal and his cast of commentators — Vince Carter, Draymond Green, Dwight Howard and TNT’s Adam Lefkoe — into a frenzy.



	According to Smeeton, the president of Authentic Studios, Season 2 of “Dunkman” will see O’Neal scouting the world to find new talent for the competition and may even incorporate undercards, à la UFC, like a 15-and-under junior dunk contest with 9-foot rims and a women’s dunking division.

	“We’ve had athletes from all over the world DMing Shaquille and the league saying, ‘I want to be in for Season 2,’ so we’re just scratching the surface,” Smeeton says.

	O’Neal adds, “We’re in talks with a lot of international countries like Poland, China and others. We’re getting calls every day. We’re going to keep it going and do small events, medium events and big events, and our ultimate goal is to partner up with the NBA and take over the Dunk Contest.”
	

	As far as his own favorite dunks, O’Neal points to his notorious dunk over the Knicks’ Chris Dudley in 1999, where he discarded him after — “I saw on the internet that that was called ‘The Most Disrespectful Dunk in History,’ and I’ll take it,” he jokes — and his absolute favorite: the Kobe alley-oop to close out the Trailblazers in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals.



	“My favorite is the Kobe lob-dunk in 2000,” offers O’Neal. “We were up 3-1 in that series and [the Trailblazers] came back to bring it to Game 7, and the fuckin’ worst thing happened where I wasn’t really playing great until late, they got up 15, and I was like, ‘Shit, here we go again.’ And then Phil Jackson was like, ‘Alright, see you guys next summer,’ and we got upset and went on a legendary comeback. I would always tell Kobe, ‘When you get to the lane instead of doing all that double-pump-fake stuff just throw it up and I’ll be there.’ And he threw it up.”

	O’Neal has been partnered with Authentic Studios since December 2015, and founded his production company, Jersey Legends, in 2020. It’s proved a fruitful partnership for O’Neal, resulting in TV productions like the acclaimed “Allen Iv3rson” docuseries for Prime, the Netflix reality show “Power Moves With Shaquille O’Neal,” the “Dunkman” league on TNT and another ABC/ESPN series shooting this fall, along with a number of scripted shows in development.

	There was even a recent (fake) viral report that O’Neal had purchased the Los Angeles Lakers, even though the Buss family actually sold the NBA team to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner for $12.5 billion. It’s proven quite the lucrative investment for the Buss family, whose father, Dr. Jerry Buss, bought the Lakers in 1979 for $67.5 million in a deal that also included the Los Angeles Kings and the Forum. Since 1980, the Lakers have won the most NBA championships in the league with 11.

	“I would love to own an NBA team and I have nothing but love and admiration for the Buss family,” O’Neal says of the deal. “One thing I learned from the Buss family is business, and I think if they did sell it would be a great business move because I know how much [Dr. Jerry Buss] bought the Lakers for. I know he’s not with us anymore, but I know he took pride in making it a family business and the family has been there through my tenure, Kobe’s tenure and LeBron’s tenure. If they did sell it for that much, then I think it was a great business move.”
	

	There is, of course, the matter of Jeanie Buss, the Lakers’ minority owner and team governor who, in a bit of “Succession”-like drama, has contested her siblings’ sale to Iger and Kushner.

	When I mention this to O’Neal, he pauses. “I never paid attention to that. There was always stuff going around, but I never got involved,” he remarks, before adding: “Actually, we should do a documentary on that!”

schema.headline: ‘Dunkman’: How Shaquille O’Neal Made Dunk Contests Great Again

title: Two People Killed In Popular Mexican Bull-Running Festival
description:
Mexican Bull-Running Festival
                          2 Killed In Stampede
body:
Mexican Bull-Running Festival
                          2 Killed In Stampede
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 25, 2026
                            7:10 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Mexican bull-running festival turned deadly over the weekend ... with two people killed and 11 others injured as raging bulls tore through the streets.
      
    
            Video circulating online shows one man being relentlessly trampled by a bull ... and in another clip, a bull roughs up a woman, throwing her onto her back.
      
    
      
      En México 🇲🇽 mujer queda desfigurada y un hombre de 29 años muere, 2 en condiciones críticas y varios heridos. Esto fue en la HUAMANTLADA 2026 en TLAXCALA. Ellos mismos se lo buscaron - ya dejen de joder y abusar de los toros. 🐂🤷‍♀️ pic.twitter.com/CvLYhmkYi8
              @Resilient_Eagle
  
    
            The man had to be dragged from the street ... and the woman somehow managed to escape on foot.
      
    
            21 bulls were released in the streets ... and the powerful animals killed 29-year-old Juan Manuel Filomeno Herrera and another man.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The horrifying incidents took place during the annual Huamantlada Festival in Tlaxcala, which is said to be the biggest bull-running event in the world.
      
    
            The festival reportedly started in 1954 and was styled after the famous running of the bulls in Pamplona, Spain.
      
    
            It's the first time in years that people have died at Huamantlada.

title: Federal Judge Rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's Bid to Get Out of Prison
description:
Ghislaine Maxwell
                          Prison Release Bid Torn To Shreds
body:
Ghislaine Maxwell
                          Prison Release Bid Torn To Shreds
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 25, 2026
                            7:59 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ghislaine Maxwell just struck out in her latest bid to get out of prison ... with a federal judge absolutely shredding her arguments.
      
    
            According to court docs obtained by TMZ, Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Maxwell's request to toss her sex trafficking conviction and 20-year prison sentence ... calling her claims "demonstrably meritless."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            And the judge didn't stop there.
      

            He said Maxwell's arguments were generally built on "speculation, distortions, and/or outright falsehoods" ... adding there wasn't a single fact she fairly put in dispute that could change the outcome of her trial.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Maxwell had argued her 2021 conviction amounted to a "complete miscarriage of justice," claiming prosecutors withheld evidence that could have cleared her and presented false testimony to jurors.
      
    
            She also pointed to materials released as part of the massive DOJ dump of Epstein-related files, arguing they amounted to substantial new evidence.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            The judge wasn't buying it ... finding most of Maxwell's claims were either barred because they'd already been raised -- or could have been raised -- on appeal, while much of her supposed new evidence was irrelevant.
      
    
            In fact, the court said some of the newly released material actually hurt Maxwell's case rather than helped it.
      
    
            Maxwell was convicted in December 2021 for her role in recruiting and grooming underage girls for Jeffrey Epstein, and she was sentenced the following year to 20 years behind bars.
      
    
            Her conviction and sentence were later upheld on appeal ... and the Supreme Court declined to hear her case.

            North West certainly doesn't lead a regular life given that her parents are Kim Kardashian and Kanye West ... but the 13-year-old rapper says she wants a regular job -- at Starbucks!
      
    
            That's right ... North sat down for a recent interview with Dazed Digital, and reporter Marios Mystidis asked North if she would be a basketball player if she wasn't a music artist.
      
    
            North responded that she had zero interest in becoming a hoops player ... and said she wanted to work at Starbucks ... and it's no joke!
      
    
            She put it this way, "I wanna work at, like, Starbucks next year. I think I can next year 'cause I'm gonna be 14, so … I think I can. I want to have a regular job, I guess."
      
    
            North went on to tell Mystidis about the worst career advice she ever received ... and it sounds like she's taking it to heart.
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            Starbucks sounds like a side quest for North, though ... she says music is her true passion, and she describes going to the studio as a "perfect day."  
      
    
            As you know, North was supposed to co-headline the "Kimokawaii" tour with Molly Santana this month, but it got canceled for unknown reasons.
      
    
            Shoot for the stars, North!!!
